gaps.spec_claim: Returns None when no project-wide semantic extraction index for C is available under proj_dir, signalling the caller that the backend is unavailable so per-file fallback extraction applies and C joins the unavailable set. Otherwise returns a dict mapping the absolute path of each indexed C source file containing at least one function to the list of that file's functions in source order, each as a (deduplicated function name, verbatim function body) pair; the dict is empty exactly when the index is available but no C source file contains any function. Function names follow the canonicalization and within-file deduplication rules shared with the extraction stage, so each name matches the identity of the corresponding extracted file and call-graph node.
gaps.actual_behavior:
The function terminates normally and returns a value of type dict. Exactly one of the following two cases holds:

Case 1 (backend unavailable): No semantic-index database exists at proj_dir/.codegraph/ nor at the parent directory of proj_dir. In this case CodeGraphExtractor.from_proj_dir(proj_dir) returns None, the conditional expression evaluates to the else-branch, and the function returns the empty dictionary {}. Formally: result == {} and len(result) == 0.

Case 2 (backend available): A semantic-index database is found at proj_dir/.codegraph/ or at the parent directory of proj_dir. CodeGraphExtractor.from_proj_dir(proj_dir) returns a valid extractor instance cg. The function returns cg.get_functions_by_file("c", proj_dir), which is a dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] mapping the absolute path of every indexed C source file that contains at least one function to an ordered list of (func_name, body) pairs in source order. Each func_name is a deduplicated identifier (repeated names within the same file receive numeric suffixes consistent with the extraction stage and call-graph node map), and each body is the verbatim source-line text of that function's span. Formally: result == {abs_path: [(name_i, body_i), ...] | abs_path is an indexed C file with 1 function} and for every key k in result, len(result[k]) >= 1.

In both cases the return type is dict and no exception is raised, provided the pre-condition on proj_dir holds. The caller (language-backend registry) may interpret an empty dict as either 'no C functions indexed' or 'backend unavailable' since both paths yield {}; the three-valued contract is satisfied at the registry level by combining this result with separate availability probes. No mutation of proj_dir or its contents occurs; no resources are leaked.
gaps.code_evidence: Line 4: return cg.get_functions_by_file("c", proj_dir) if cg else {}
gaps.trigger_condition: Condition B explicitly requires that when no project-wide semantic extraction index is available, the function returns None to signal backend unavailability (so per-file fallback extraction applies and C joins the unavailable set). However, the code's else-branch returns the empty dict {} instead of None. This conflates two distinct situations: (1) backend unavailable (should be None) and (2) backend available but no C file contains any function (should be {}). A caller checking `result is None` to trigger fallback extraction will never see None, breaking the three-valued contract described in the specification.
